newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to renovate She-Wolf, symbol of Rome.
newsitem.headline: Italy to renovate She-Wolf, symbol of Rome.

text.p: Rome's council said on Thursday it would renovate a prized statue of the She-Wolf which according to legend reared the city's founder, Romulus and his twin Remus.
The work, believed to date from the fifth century BC, shows the She-Wolf suckling the infants. It is considered the oldest bronze in Italy and has not been restored for some 500 years.
The statue, which has symbolised the Eternal City for centuries, was recently moved indoors from its place in Rome's Campidoglio Square because of damage from pollution. It is now kept in a museum.
Officials said they hoped the restauration, expected to cost some 230 million lire ($135,000) and to take eight months, would yield clues about its origins.

According to popular legend, the grandfather of Romulus and Remus was deposed by his brother, who then tried to kill the twins by abandoning them in the river Tiber. They were saved by the She-Wolf after being washed ashore.
Romulus went on to found Rome in about 753 BC. ($1=1,700 lire)
